_comment: The committed gfx942 OBJECT BUDGET -- what every default-configuration code object is
allowed to be. Asserted by `asm_audit.py --contract` from scripts/build_gfx942.sh on every
build; re-blessed with `--bless`, which rewrites everything below `geom_profiles`.
WHY A COMMITTED FILE AND NOT A THRESHOLD. build_gfx942.sh used to carry this table as four
lines of header comment, and it was stale: it claimed interp_prefill spill 6 where the
measured ISA figure is 4127 scratch ops (126 by the note, which only covers the interpreter
kernel itself). A number a build prints is a number nobody diffs. A number in the tree moves
in a `git diff` and has to be explained in a commit message, which is the whole point --
the same property crates/devgen/src/dispatch_audit.rs was built for on the emit side.
A ROW IS ONLY COMPARED WHEN THE AXES MATCH. `defines` is the exact `-D` set the row was
blessed from; a PLOW_OCC4 / PLOW_DECODE_BATCH / PLOW_ROWS_ONLY build compiles a different
object and is checked only by the rules that need no baseline (the geometry markers, the
note-vs-ISA spill disagreement, and head-dim arm coverage).
FIELDS
vgpr agpr lds occ   the resource table, from the object's AMDHSA note. `occ` is computed:
min(512 VGPR/SIMD over the 8-granule allocation, LDS workgroups x
waves / 4 SIMDs). `.vgpr_count` is ALREADY the unified arch+acc total
on gfx90a and later and `.agpr_count` is its accumulator SUBSET.
meta_spill          `.vgpr_spill_count` from the note. Recorded to be DISBELIEVED: it
covers only the kernel symbols, and every outlined body -- plow_exec,
d_gemm_glu, d_flash_prefill<D> -- has no note at all.
isa_spill           scratch_load_*/scratch_store_* over EVERY symbol. This is the budget;
exceeding it fails, undercutting it asks to be re-blessed.
unmetered_spill     the part of isa_spill in symbols with no note, i.e. the part
`.vgpr_spill_count` cannot see by construction.
bpermute lds16      the two advisory counts (LDS crossbar, 2-byte LDS reads), recorded so
a change in either shows up in the diff even though neither fails.
arms                d_flash_* template instantiations that survived inlining, by head dim.
Removing a dispatch arm removes its instantiation from this set.
geom                which geometry profile the object compiled. Shared, because most rows
compile identical geometry and one knob moving should be one changed
line rather than forty.
